nodes.title: Cloudera Base on premises

formerly: Cloudera Data Platform Private Cloud Base

nodes.title: Cloudera Data Catalog
nodes.description: Catalogue service over SDX metadata for searching assets, viewing Atlas lineage and running profilers that collect statistics and detect sensitive data.

nodes.title: Cloudera Data Engineering
nodes.description: Containerised, autoscaling Apache Spark service with job management and an embedded Apache Airflow for orchestrating pipelines.

nodes.title: Cloudera Data Flow
nodes.description: Managed Apache NiFi service for building, deploying and autoscaling flows that collect, route and transform data from files, databases, APIs and streams.
formerly: Cloudera DataFlow for the Public Cloud

nodes.title: Cloudera Data Lineage
nodes.description: SaaS metadata and lineage service that harvests ETL tools, databases and BI reports to map dependencies across systems inside and outside Cloudera.

nodes.title: Cloudera Data Services on premises
nodes.description: Kubernetes-based deployment of the Data Engineering, Data Warehouse and Cloudera AI services on customer infrastructure, attached to a Cloudera Base cluster.

nodes.title: Cloudera Data Visualization
nodes.description: Built-in BI tool for dashboards and applications over Cloudera warehouses and AI projects, including an AI visual that answers natural-language questions.

nodes.title: Cloudera Data Warehouse
nodes.description: Containerised SQL service in which teams create isolated, autoscaling Virtual Warehouses running Impala, Hive LLAP or Trino over shared data lake tables.

nodes.title: Cloudera Iceberg REST Catalog
nodes.description: Implementation of the Iceberg REST catalogue API on the Hive Metastore that lets external engines read Cloudera-governed Iceberg tables using short-lived, scoped storage credentials.

nodes.title: Apache Iceberg in Cloudera
nodes.description: Native Apache Iceberg v2 table support across Spark, Hive, Impala, Trino, Flink and NiFi, including time travel, partition evolution and row-level changes.

nodes.title: Cloudera Lakehouse Optimizer
nodes.description: Policy-driven service that schedules and runs Iceberg table maintenance such as compaction, snapshot expiry and statistics collection.

nodes.title: Cloudera Observability
nodes.description: Monitoring and analysis service for Cloudera workloads that shows job and query performance, recommends fixes and reports resource use and cost by workload.

nodes.title: Cloudera on cloud
nodes.description: Cloudera's platform running in the customer's AWS, Azure or Google Cloud account, with a Cloudera-hosted Management Console that creates environments, data lakes and Data Hub clusters.

nodes.title: Cloudera Operational Database
nodes.description: Autoscaling Apache HBase service with Apache Phoenix SQL for low-latency reads and writes on large, sparse operational datasets.

nodes.title: Apache Ozone in Cloudera
nodes.description: S3-compatible, scale-out object store for on-premises Cloudera clusters, intended to replace HDFS for very large file counts.

nodes.title: Cloudera Replication Manager
nodes.description: Service that schedules replication of HDFS, Hive, Iceberg and HBase data and metadata between clusters and to cloud storage.

nodes.title: Cloudera Shared Data Experience (SDX)
nodes.description: Common security and governance layer, built on Apache Ranger, Apache Atlas and Apache Knox, applied to every engine on the same data.

nodes.title: Cloudera Streaming Analytics
nodes.description: Apache Flink distribution with SQL Stream Builder, a console for writing continuous SQL jobs and materialised views over streams.

nodes.title: Cloudera Streams Messaging
nodes.description: Cloudera's Apache Kafka distribution with Schema Registry, Streams Messaging Manager, Streams Replication Manager and Cruise Control.

nodes.title: Coalesce Transform
nodes.description: Metadata-driven, column-aware workspace for designing and deploying SQL transformation pipelines on Snowflake, Databricks and other cloud platforms, using reusable node types.

nodes.title: Collibra AI Command Center
nodes.description: Registry and control plane for AI use cases, models and agents that links each one to its data, policies and assessments and tracks production trust signals.

nodes.title: Collibra Data Access
nodes.description: Manages access requests, masking, row filtering and role-based grants centrally and provisions them into Snowflake, Databricks and BigQuery.

nodes.title: Collibra Data Catalog
nodes.description: Searchable inventory of data assets across warehouses, lakes, applications and BI tools, built from automatically harvested metadata and enriched with descriptions and classifications.

nodes.title: Collibra Data Governance
nodes.description: Governance workspace for business glossaries, ownership and stewardship roles, policies and the workflows that route approvals and issues to stewards.

nodes.title: Collibra Data Lineage
nodes.description: Automatically extracts lineage from SQL, ETL tools and BI reports and shows it at table and column level across systems.

nodes.title: Collibra Data Quality & Observability
nodes.description: Profiles data, generates and runs quality rules, and monitors tables for schema changes, missing or duplicate records and other anomalies, publishing scores to the catalogue.

nodes.title: Comet ML
nodes.description: ML experiment management (tracking, artefacts, model registry and production monitoring) together with Opik for tracing, evaluating and optimising LLM applications and agents.

nodes.title: Confluent Cloud
nodes.description: Fully managed Apache Kafka service on AWS, Azure and Google Cloud, with managed connectors, Schema Registry, Stream Governance and cluster linking.

nodes.title: Confluent Cloud for Apache Flink
nodes.description: Serverless Apache Flink service for continuous SQL and Table API processing over Kafka topics, with autoscaling and built-in functions.

nodes.title: Confluent Intelligence
nodes.description: Confluent Cloud's AI layer. It runs event-driven agents on Flink, serves the latest topic state to external agents over MCP, and applies built-in ML functions and model calls to streams.

nodes.title: Confluent Platform
nodes.description: Self-managed Kafka distribution for on-premises and private cloud, with connectors, Schema Registry, Flink and management tooling.

nodes.title: Confluent Tableflow
nodes.description: Materialises Kafka topics and their schemas as Apache Iceberg or Delta Lake tables, taking care of type conversion, schema evolution, compaction and catalogue sync.

nodes.title: Credo AI Governance Platform
nodes.description: Keeps a registry of AI systems, agents, models and vendors and turns regulations and policies into controls, risk assessments and evidence.

nodes.title: Cube Cloud
nodes.description: Managed semantic layer and agentic analytics platform that defines governed metrics once and serves them to BI tools, applications and AI agents through SQL and chat APIs.

nodes.title: Cube Core
nodes.description: Semantic layer that defines data models and metrics once and serves them through SQL, REST and GraphQL APIs with caching and pre-aggregations.

nodes.title: Cyera DSPM
nodes.description: Agentless discovery and AI-based classification of sensitive data across cloud, SaaS and on-premises stores, showing who and what can reach it and which exposures matter.

nodes.title: Dagster
nodes.description: Data orchestrator built around software-defined assets, where you declare the data assets you want and their dependencies and Dagster schedules and tracks them.

nodes.title: Dagster+
nodes.description: Managed control plane for Dagster's asset-based orchestration, with an asset catalogue, branch deployments, cost and performance insights and alerting.

nodes.title: Dask
nodes.description: Python library that scales NumPy, pandas and custom Python code in parallel across cores or a cluster.

nodes.title: Data Contract CLI
nodes.description: Command-line tool that lints data contracts, tests live data against them, detects breaking changes and generates code and documentation from them.

nodes.title: data.world
nodes.description: Data catalogue and governance service built on a knowledge graph, which links technical assets to business concepts.

nodes.title: Unity Catalog attribute-based access control (ABAC)
nodes.description: Policies attached at catalogue, schema or table level that use governed tags and user attributes to apply row filters, column masks and dynamic grants automatically.

nodes.title: Agent Bricks
nodes.description: Databricks' platform for developing agents. It brings together agent hosting, sandboxed code execution, memory, MCP tools, retrieval, tracing, evaluation and governed model access.

nodes.title: Databricks Agent Evaluation (MLflow GenAI evaluation)
nodes.description: Evaluates agents and LLM applications against datasets, using built-in and custom scorers, LLM judges and human feedback, and also monitors production traces.

nodes.title: Databricks Agent Runtime and Agent Bricks CLI
nodes.description: Serverless hosting for code-based agents on Databricks Apps, with durable run state, an authenticated endpoint, a service-principal identity and MLflow tracing, deployed with the agentbricks CLI.

nodes.title: Databricks agentic code converter
nodes.description: A Genie Code-based migration project that converts T-SQL, Snowflake, Redshift, Oracle, BigQuery and Teradata SQL into Databricks SQL or DataFrame notebooks.

nodes.title: Databricks AI/BI dashboards
nodes.description: Built-in dashboards with AI-assisted authoring, cross-filtering and drill-through. They can be shared at account level, sent on schedules by email or Slack, and embedded in external applications.

nodes.title: Databricks AI Functions
nodes.description: SQL and Python functions that call models over table data. They include ai_query, ai_extract, ai_classify, ai_summarize, ai_translate, ai_mask, ai_forecast and ai_similarity, with ai_search, ai_prep_search and ai_transcribe in Beta.

nodes.title: Databricks ai_parse_document
nodes.description: An AI Function that extracts text, tables and layout elements from PDFs, images and office documents stored in volumes, returning structured output.

nodes.title: Databricks AI Runtime
nodes.description: Serverless GPU compute for deep learning, used to train and fine-tune models on one or many GPUs with PyTorch DDP and FSDP, DeepSpeed or Ray.

nodes.title: Databricks AI Search
nodes.description: A managed vector and full-text search service. Delta Sync indexes stay in step with source tables and can compute embeddings, and hybrid retrieval is supported.

nodes.title: Databricks Apps
nodes.description: Serverless hosting for Python and Node.js web applications (for example Streamlit, Dash, Gradio and React) that run inside the workspace with Unity Catalog, SQL warehouse and OAuth integration.

nodes.title: Databricks Auto Loader
nodes.description: A Structured Streaming source (cloudFiles) that discovers new files in cloud storage and processes each one exactly once, with schema inference, schema evolution and a rescued-data column.

nodes.title: Databricks automatic identity management
nodes.description: Synchronises users, groups and service principals from Microsoft Entra ID or Okta on demand, without configuring SCIM provisioning. It works alongside SSO, OAuth and service principals.

nodes.title: Databricks AutoML
nodes.description: Generates baseline classification, regression and forecasting models through a UI or Python API, and produces editable notebooks for each trial.

nodes.title: Databricks budgets
nodes.description: Account-level spend tracking at list price, filtered by workspace, resource type and tags. You set monthly thresholds with email alerts and, for Unity Gateway, optional per-user blocking.

nodes.title: Databricks Catalog Explorer
nodes.description: The workspace UI for browsing and managing Unity Catalog assets. It shows schemas, permissions, lineage, popularity, table health indicators and AI-generated comments.

nodes.title: Databricks catalog federation
nodes.description: Mounts external catalogues such as Hive metastore, AWS Glue, Snowflake Horizon and Salesforce Data 360 as foreign catalogs, read from object storage under Unity Catalog governance.

nodes.title: Databricks change data feed
nodes.description: Records row-level inserts, updates and deletes on Delta tables so downstream jobs and streams can read only the changes.

nodes.title: Databricks classic compute (Databricks Runtime clusters)
nodes.description: All-purpose and job clusters, plus instance pools, running Databricks Runtime in the customer's cloud account. You choose instance types, autoscaling and access mode.

nodes.title: Databricks Clean Rooms
nodes.description: Isolated serverless environments where up to ten organisations share data through OpenSharing and run notebooks that every party has approved. No party sees the others' underlying data.

nodes.title: Databricks compliance security profile
nodes.description: A workspace setting that applies a hardened, FIPS-validated compute image, enhanced security monitoring and encrypted egress, required for HIPAA, PCI-DSS, FedRAMP and similar regulated data.

nodes.title: Databricks Connect
nodes.description: A client library built on Spark Connect. Python, Scala and R DataFrame code written in an IDE or application runs on remote Databricks compute, including serverless.

nodes.title: Databricks customer-managed keys
nodes.description: Customer-held cloud KMS keys that encrypt control-plane data (notebooks, secrets, queries), workspace storage and, at catalogue level, Unity Catalog managed data.

nodes.title: Databricks Data Classification
nodes.description: A serverless agent that scans Unity Catalog tables incrementally, detects sensitive data such as PII and payment-card data, and tags the columns.

nodes.title: Databricks data profiling
nodes.description: Computes profile and drift metrics for a table over time as snapshot, time-series or inference profiles, and stores them in Delta tables with a generated dashboard.

nodes.title: Databricks Declarative Automation Bundles
nodes.description: A Databricks CLI feature that defines jobs, pipelines, dashboards, apps, serving endpoints, AI Search, Lakebase and other resources in YAML with per-target settings. The CLI then validates, plans and deploys them from CI/CD.

nodes.title: Delta Lake on Databricks
nodes.description: Databricks' managed implementation of Delta Lake tables, with ACID commits, MERGE, UPDATE and DELETE, schema enforcement, time travel, deletion vectors and type widening.

nodes.title: Databricks Discover
nodes.description: A curated browsing page that groups governed tables, dashboards, notebooks and Genie Agents into business domains and subdomains, with highlighted assets chosen by admins and AI recommendations.

nodes.title: Databricks data quality monitoring anomaly detection
nodes.description: Monitors every table in a schema with one setting. It learns each table's update and volume patterns, flags late or incomplete tables, and suggests root causes using lineage.

nodes.title: Databricks Excel Add-in
nodes.description: A Microsoft Excel add-in for querying governed Databricks tables and metric views from a workbook.

nodes.title: Databricks Feature Store
nodes.description: A feature registry in Unity Catalog that stores features in primary-keyed Delta tables, with point-in-time training set creation, automatic lookup at inference and lineage to models.

nodes.title: Databricks Feature Views
nodes.description: Declarative feature definitions, including time-windowed aggregations over batch, streaming and request-time data, for which Databricks builds and runs the pipelines.

nodes.title: Databricks Foundation Model APIs
nodes.description: Databricks-hosted proprietary and open language and embedding models, available pay-per-token or with provisioned throughput. They are exposed as governed model services in the system.ai schema.

nodes.title: Databricks Free Edition
nodes.description: A no-cost, serverless-only, quota-limited Databricks environment for learning and experiments. It includes notebooks, SQL, Lakeflow, dashboards, Genie, Genie Code and Lakebase.

nodes.title: Genie Agents
nodes.description: Domain-specific chat interfaces that analysts curate with tables, metric views, example SQL and instructions. They answer business questions in natural language with SQL, tables and charts.

nodes.title: Genie Code
nodes.description: An AI coding and data agent in notebooks, the SQL editor, the pipelines editor, dashboards and MLflow. It plans, writes and runs code, fixes errors and builds pipelines and dashboards, using Unity Catalog context and the user's permissions.

nodes.title: Genie One
nodes.description: A simplified interface for business users that combines chat across governed data, dashboards and apps in one place, available in the browser, desktop, Excel and Google Sheets.

nodes.title: Databricks Git folders
nodes.description: Workspace folders backed by a Git repository. Users clone, branch, commit, merge and resolve conflicts from the UI, the API or Git CLI commands.

nodes.title: Databricks Governance Hub
nodes.description: An account-level console that brings together data health and governance coverage, tag usage, AI usage and spend, and cost drivers, with recommended actions.

nodes.title: Databricks governed tags
nodes.description: Account-level tag definitions with controlled values and assignment permissions, applied to Unity Catalog objects and workspace assets and used by ABAC, classification and cost reporting.

nodes.title: Databricks Iceberg reads (UniForm)
nodes.description: Generates Iceberg metadata asynchronously for Delta tables so that Iceberg clients can read them without copying the data.

nodes.title: Unity Catalog Iceberg REST Catalog API
nodes.description: An Iceberg REST catalogue endpoint with credential vending. Spark, Flink, Trino, Snowflake and other engines can use it to read and write Unity Catalog tables.

nodes.title: Databricks inference tables
nodes.description: Logs requests and responses from serving endpoints, foundation model calls and agents to Unity Catalog Delta tables for monitoring, audit and retraining.

nodes.title: Agent Bricks Knowledge Assistant and Supervisor Agent
nodes.description: No-code agents. Knowledge Assistant answers questions over documents with citations, and Supervisor Agent coordinates Genie Agents, tables, AI Search indexes, MCP servers and other agents.

nodes.title: Lakebase
nodes.description: Fully managed Postgres in the Databricks platform. Compute is separate from storage, and it offers autoscaling, scale-to-zero, copy-on-write branching, instant point-in-time restore and read replicas.

nodes.title: Lakebridge
nodes.description: A Databricks Labs migration toolkit. It assesses legacy warehouse and ETL estates, transpiles their SQL and ETL code to Databricks, and reconciles the migrated data against the source.

nodes.title: Lakeflow Connect
nodes.description: Managed connectors that ingest data incrementally from SaaS applications, databases (including change data capture), file sources and message buses into Unity Catalog tables, running on serverless Lakeflow pipelines.

nodes.title: Lakeflow Designer
nodes.description: A visual, no-code canvas where analysts build data preparation flows from operators or natural-language prompts. The flows are backed by generated code governed in Unity Catalog.

nodes.title: Lakeflow Jobs
nodes.description: Built-in orchestrator that runs dependency graphs of notebooks, pipelines, SQL, dbt and other tasks on schedules or on file-arrival, table-update and continuous triggers, with retries and loops.

nodes.title: Lakeflow pipelines
nodes.description: A declarative framework in which you define streaming tables, materialised views and flows in SQL or Python. The platform then works out dependencies, incremental refresh, retries and infrastructure.

nodes.title: Lakeguard
nodes.description: Isolation technology that sandboxes each user's code and UDFs away from the Spark engine and from other users, so shared compute can enforce Unity Catalog row filters and column masks.

nodes.title: Lakehouse Federation (query federation)
nodes.description: Read-only queries against external databases such as PostgreSQL, Oracle, SQL Server, Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift and Teradata through Unity Catalog foreign catalogs, with query pushdown.

nodes.title: Databricks Lakehouse Real-Time
nodes.description: A serverless SQL warehouse type tuned for sub-second reads of Unity Catalog tables by many concurrent users and applications.

nodes.title: Databricks liquid clustering
nodes.description: A data layout method that clusters table files by key columns you can change at any time, replacing partitioning and Z-ordering. With CLUSTER BY AUTO, Databricks chooses the keys from query history.

nodes.title: Databricks managed disaster recovery
nodes.description: Replicates Unity Catalog metadata, managed table data and workspace assets to a secondary region, behind a stable URL that survives failover.

nodes.title: Unity Catalog managed Iceberg tables
nodes.description: Apache Iceberg tables (v1 to v3) that Unity Catalog manages, with compaction, snapshot expiry and liquid clustering. Databricks and external engines can read and write them through the Iceberg REST catalogue.

nodes.title: Databricks managed MCP servers
nodes.description: Hosted Model Context Protocol servers that expose Unity Catalog functions, AI Search indexes, Genie Agents and Genie One to agents as tools. External MCP servers can also be registered as Unity Catalog MCP services.

nodes.title: Managed MLflow on Databricks
nodes.description: MLflow 3 hosted by Databricks, with experiment and run tracking, logged models, prompt management and deployment jobs, all integrated with Unity Catalog permissions and lineage.

nodes.title: Databricks Marketplace
nodes.description: An exchange for publishing and finding datasets, AI models, notebooks, apps and MCP servers, either publicly or through private exchanges, delivered with OpenSharing.

nodes.title: Unity Catalog metric views
nodes.description: YAML- or SQL-defined semantic objects that keep measures apart from dimensions. They are registered in Unity Catalog and queried from SQL, dashboards, Genie and external BI tools.

nodes.title: MLflow Tracing on Databricks
nodes.description: Records each step of agent and LLM calls, including inputs, outputs, latency, tokens and feedback, and stores the traces in Unity Catalog tables that can be queried with SQL.

nodes.title: Databricks Model Serving
nodes.description: Serverless CPU and GPU endpoints for serving custom MLflow models, Databricks-hosted foundation models and external models in real time, with traffic splitting between model versions.

nodes.title: Models in Unity Catalog
nodes.description: The MLflow model registry hosted in Unity Catalog, with versions, aliases, permissions, tags and lineage to training data and features shared across workspaces.

nodes.title: Databricks notebooks
nodes.description: Collaborative notebooks with Python, SQL, Scala and R cells, comments, version history, widgets and visualisations that can be scheduled as jobs.

nodes.title: Databricks Online Feature Store
nodes.description: A Lakebase-backed store that publishes feature tables for millisecond lookups by Model Serving endpoints and feature serving endpoints.

nodes.title: Databricks OpenSharing
nodes.description: Live sharing of tables, views, materialised views, metric views, volumes, models and notebooks with other Databricks accounts, or tabular data with any client through an open protocol, without copying.

nodes.title: Databricks Photon
nodes.description: Databricks' native C++ vectorised execution engine. It runs Spark SQL and DataFrame operations on columnar batches and falls back to Spark for operations it does not support.

nodes.title: Lakeflow pipelines expectations
nodes.description: Declarative data quality constraints on pipeline datasets. For each failing record you choose to warn, drop it or fail the update, and the results are recorded in the pipeline event log.

nodes.title: Databricks predictive optimization
nodes.description: Runs OPTIMIZE, VACUUM and ANALYZE automatically on Unity Catalog managed tables and chooses liquid clustering keys, based on how each table is used.

nodes.title: Private Link for Databricks
nodes.description: AWS PrivateLink, Azure Private Link and Private Service Connect connectivity for front-end access, classic compute to the control plane, and inbound access to serverless services such as Lakebase and Zerobus Ingest.

nodes.title: Secrets in Unity Catalog
nodes.description: Credentials stored as governed Unity Catalog securables under a catalog.schema.secret name, with grants and audit.

nodes.title: Databricks serverless compute
nodes.description: Databricks-managed, versionless compute for notebooks, jobs and pipelines. It starts quickly, scales automatically and is billed in DBUs per use.

nodes.title: Databricks serverless egress control
nodes.description: Account-level network policies that limit which destinations serverless compute, apps and model serving can reach, used with network connectivity configurations and private endpoint rules.

nodes.title: Databricks serverless usage policies
nodes.description: Sets of tags applied automatically to the serverless usage of the users assigned to a policy, so that spend from notebooks, jobs, pipelines, serving, apps and Lakebase can be attributed.

nodes.title: Databricks spatial SQL (GEOMETRY and GEOGRAPHY)
nodes.description: Native GEOMETRY and GEOGRAPHY types with ST_ functions for constructing, measuring, relating and transforming spatial data, plus H3 functions.

nodes.title: Databricks SQL
nodes.description: The data warehousing product on the lakehouse. It includes the SQL editor, queries, ANSI SQL engine, SQL transformations, materialised views and BI connectivity, running on SQL warehouses.

nodes.title: Databricks SQL alerts
nodes.description: Scheduled queries that evaluate a condition and send email, Slack or webhook notifications when it is met.

nodes.title: Databricks JDBC, ODBC and ADBC drivers
nodes.description: Client drivers and connectors (JDBC, ODBC, ADBC, Python, Go and Node.js) plus the SQL Statement Execution REST API, used to query Databricks SQL warehouses from tools and code.

nodes.title: Databricks SQL warehouses (serverless, pro and classic)
nodes.description: Compute for Databricks SQL in serverless, pro or classic form. Serverless warehouses start in seconds and use intelligent workload management to scale and queue queries.

nodes.title: Databricks system tables
nodes.description: Databricks-hosted tables in the system catalog that cover billing, audit, lineage, compute, query history, jobs, pipelines, serving, MLflow, classification, data quality and Lakebase activity.

nodes.title: Databricks table clone (shallow and deep clone)
nodes.description: Copies a table at a given version. A shallow clone copies only metadata and points at the source files, while a deep clone copies the data as well.

nodes.title: Databricks Terraform provider
nodes.description: A Terraform provider (databricks/databricks) that manages workspaces, Unity Catalog objects, permissions, compute, jobs and other Databricks resources as code.

nodes.title: Unity Catalog
nodes.description: The account-wide catalogue and governance layer for tables, volumes, functions, models, AI services and connections. It provides a three-level namespace, SQL privileges, audit and workspace bindings.

nodes.title: Unity Catalog functions (UDFs)
nodes.description: SQL, Python, Scala and Java user-defined functions registered and governed in Unity Catalog. They run on serverless and standard compute with sandboxing.

nodes.title: Unity Catalog data lineage
nodes.description: Captures table- and column-level lineage automatically for queries, notebooks, jobs, pipelines, dashboards and models. External sources and BI tools can be registered so they appear in the same graph.

nodes.title: Unity Catalog managed tables
nodes.description: Delta or Iceberg tables whose storage location, file layout, maintenance and lifecycle Unity Catalog manages, including on Databricks-managed default storage.

nodes.title: Unity Gateway
nodes.description: A governance and routing layer in Unity Catalog for model, MCP and agent traffic, with provider fallbacks, rate and consumption limits, guardrails, inference logging and budgets.

nodes.title: Databricks VARIANT data type
nodes.description: A binary type for semi-structured data such as JSON that is queried without a fixed schema, with shredding into columns for faster reads.

nodes.title: Unity Catalog volumes
nodes.description: Governed, path-addressable storage for non-tabular files such as documents, images, libraries and landing data. Volumes can be managed or external.

nodes.title: Zerobus Ingest
nodes.description: A serverless push API that writes records straight into Unity Catalog Delta tables. Clients can use gRPC SDKs, REST, OpenTelemetry (OTLP), MQTT or Kafka-compatible producers, and no message broker is needed.

nodes.title: DataHub
nodes.description: Metadata platform and data catalogue with search, column-level lineage, glossary, ownership, quality assertions and an event-driven metadata model.

nodes.title: DataHub Cloud
nodes.description: Managed, extended edition of the open-source DataHub metadata platform that adds data observability assertions, AI documentation, access request workflows and an AI assistant.

nodes.title: Dataiku
nodes.description: Collaborative platform for data preparation, visual and code-based machine learning, AutoML, deployment, monitoring and building AI agents, used by both analysts and data scientists.

nodes.title: Dataiku LLM Mesh
nodes.description: Abstraction layer that routes calls from Dataiku projects to many LLM providers, with quotas, cost tracking, PII screening and monitoring.

nodes.title: DataRobot AI Platform
nodes.description: Platform for building, deploying, monitoring and governing predictive models, generative AI applications and agents, known for its AutoML.

nodes.title: dbt Catalog
nodes.description: Searchable catalogue of the models, sources, metrics and exposures in dbt projects, with lineage, documentation and run health.

nodes.title: dbt Charts
nodes.description: Dashboard product in which each dashboard is a YAML file of queries, charts and layout, kept beside dbt models and validated in CI, with a hosted platform for editing, sharing and chat.

nodes.title: dbt Copilot
nodes.description: AI assistant in the dbt platform that drafts models, tests, documentation, semantic models and SQL from natural language.

nodes.title: dbt Core (v1.x)
nodes.description: Python framework for SQL and Python transformations as version-controlled models, with dependency resolution, tests, documentation and lineage.

nodes.title: dbt v2 engine
nodes.description: Rust-based dbt v2 engine, distributed as "dbt", that parses and understands SQL across warehouse dialects, so it can catch errors and resolve dependencies before anything runs in the warehouse.

nodes.title: dbt Lake Compute
nodes.description: Hosted serverless DuckDB-based compute that runs dbt models directly against Apache Iceberg tables, either alongside a warehouse or as a project's main engine.

nodes.title: dbt OSS
nodes.description: Open-source distribution of the Rust-based dbt v2 engine, which parses and compiles dbt projects much faster and checks them against a strict language specification.

nodes.title: dbt platform
nodes.description: Hosted service for developing, testing, scheduling and deploying dbt transformation projects, with a browser IDE, a visual editor, job scheduling, CI on pull requests and environments.

nodes.title: dbt Semantic Layer
nodes.description: Defines metrics and semantic models alongside dbt models, using MetricFlow, and serves them through APIs to BI tools, spreadsheets and AI assistants.

nodes.title: Debezium
nodes.description: Log-based change data capture platform that streams row-level changes from databases such as PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, Oracle and MongoDB.

nodes.title: Delta Lake
nodes.description: Open table format and libraries that add ACID transactions, schema enforcement, time travel and row-level updates to Parquet files.

nodes.title: OpenSharing protocol
nodes.description: Open protocol, the successor to Delta Sharing, for sharing live tables, unstructured data, AI models and agent skills with other organisations and tools without copying the data.

nodes.title: Denodo Platform
nodes.description: Logical data management and virtualisation platform that presents many sources as one governed semantic model and pushes queries down to them.

nodes.title: dlt (data load tool)
nodes.description: Python library for writing extract-and-load pipelines that infer and evolve schemas, load incrementally and write to warehouses, lakes and lakehouse tables.

nodes.title: Docling
nodes.description: Library that converts PDFs, Office files, HTML and images into structured text, tables and layout for retrieval and AI pipelines.

nodes.title: Domino Enterprise AI Platform
nodes.description: Governed workbench for code-first data science that provides compute and GPUs across clouds and on premises, with experiment reproducibility, model deployment, governance and cost controls.

nodes.title: Domo
nodes.description: Cloud BI platform with its own connectors, drag-and-drop Magic ETL, dashboards, low-code App Studio, workflows and embedded analytics.

nodes.title: Dremio Cloud
nodes.description: Managed lakehouse query service built on Apache Iceberg, with an Iceberg catalogue, automatic query acceleration and an AI semantic layer.

nodes.title: DuckDB
nodes.description: In-process analytical SQL database that runs inside an application or notebook and queries local files, object storage and lakehouse tables quickly on one machine.

nodes.title: DuckLake
nodes.description: Lakehouse table format that keeps data in Parquet files on object storage and all table metadata in an ordinary SQL database.

nodes.title: DVC (Data Version Control)
nodes.description: Command-line tool that versions datasets and models alongside code in Git, storing the large files in remote storage.

nodes.title: Elastic Cloud
nodes.description: Managed Elasticsearch, offered serverless or as hosted clusters, for full-text, log and vector search, with observability and security solutions and an agent builder.

nodes.title: Estuary
nodes.description: Data movement platform that combines CDC, streaming and batch pipelines, backfilling history and then capturing changes into collections stored in the customer's bucket.

nodes.title: Evidently
nodes.description: Python library for evaluating and monitoring ML models and LLM applications, with data drift, data quality and model quality reports and tests.

nodes.title: Experian Aperture Data Studio

nodes.title: Snowflake Fail-safe

nodes.title: Snowflake Feature Store
nodes.description: Python APIs and objects for defining entities and feature views (as Dynamic Tables or views), generating point-in-time correct training sets and retrieving features for batch inference.

nodes.title: Snowflake generation 2 standard warehouses
nodes.description: The newer generation of standard warehouses, running on faster hardware with optimisations for DELETE, UPDATE, MERGE and table scans.

nodes.title: Snowflake geospatial data types and functions
nodes.description: GEOGRAPHY and GEOMETRY types with spatial functions, H3 indexing and spatial joins in SQL.

nodes.title: Snowflake Git integration (Git repository objects)
nodes.description: Syncs remote Git repositories into Snowflake as repository clones, so code can be run with EXECUTE IMMEDIATE FROM and Workspaces, notebooks and Streamlit apps can commit and push.

nodes.title: Snowflake Horizon Catalog
nodes.description: Snowflake's built-in catalogue and governance layer, covering object discovery, tagging, policies, quality, lineage, access history and Iceberg catalogue services for Snowflake and external data.

nodes.title: Snowflake Horizon Context
nodes.description: A layer of Horizon Catalog that gathers external metadata and lineage, enriches it with semantics, popularity and AI descriptions, and exposes it to agents and BI tools through search and MCP.

nodes.title: Snowflake Horizon Iceberg REST Catalog API
nodes.description: An Apache Polaris-based Iceberg REST catalogue endpoint in each account that lets Spark, Trino, Flink, DuckDB, PyIceberg and other engines read and write Snowflake-managed Iceberg tables under Snowflake RBAC.

nodes.title: Snowflake hybrid tables (Unistore)
nodes.description: A row-oriented table type with enforced primary, unique and foreign keys, indexes and row locking, for low-latency point reads and writes in the same engine as analytical tables.

nodes.title: Apache Iceberg tables in Snowflake
nodes.description: Tables stored as Parquet files with Apache Iceberg metadata, managed either by Snowflake as catalogue or by an external catalogue, in customer storage or in Snowflake storage.

nodes.title: Snowflake Intent-Driven Governance
nodes.description: A review-first CoCo workflow that turns a governance goal stated in plain language into a scope, a governance specification and SQL for tags and protections, which a person approves before it runs.

nodes.title: Snowflake interactive tables and interactive warehouses
nodes.description: A table type and a matching warehouse type built for sub-second, highly concurrent queries such as user-facing dashboards and data APIs.

nodes.title: Snowflake Internal Marketplace (organisational listings)
nodes.description: A private marketplace inside a Snowflake organisation where teams publish organisational listings as data products for discovery and access requests by other accounts.

nodes.title: Snowflake listings (with Cross-Cloud Auto-Fulfillment)
nodes.description: Package a share, app or service with descriptive metadata as a data product for chosen accounts, replicating it automatically to consumers in other regions and clouds.

nodes.title: Snowflake-managed MCP server
nodes.description: A Snowflake object that exposes Cortex Agents, Cortex Analyst, Cortex Search, SQL execution and custom functions as Model Context Protocol tools to external AI clients under RBAC.

nodes.title: Snowflake micro-partitioned table storage
nodes.description: Stores standard tables in immutable, compressed, columnar micro-partitions with per-partition statistics that Snowflake manages, giving ACID transactions and partition pruning.

nodes.title: Snowflake Marketplace
nodes.description: A public catalogue where providers publish free, paid or trial listings of data, Native Apps, Cortex Knowledge Extensions and agents, and consumers subscribe to them.

nodes.title: Snowflake masking policies
nodes.description: Schema-level policies that mask, tokenise or reveal column values at query time depending on role, other context or tags, including external tokenisation through external functions.

nodes.title: Snowflake materialized views
nodes.description: Stores the results of a single-table query and keeps them up to date automatically in the background, so queries read precomputed results.

nodes.title: Snowflake ML Experiments
nodes.description: Records runs with parameters, metrics, artefacts and logs inside experiments, with autologging for common libraries and side-by-side comparison in Snowsight.

nodes.title: Snowflake ML Functions
nodes.description: SQL-callable model classes for time-series forecasting, anomaly detection, classification and top insights, which train and run without ML code.

nodes.title: Snowflake ML Jobs
nodes.description: Submits Python functions, files or code bundles from any IDE or from SQL to run as jobs on Container Runtime compute pools, including on multiple nodes.

nodes.title: Snowflake ML Observability (model monitors)
nodes.description: Model monitor objects that compute drift, performance and statistical metrics from logged inference data, with dashboards and threshold alerts.

nodes.title: Snowflake Model Registry
nodes.description: Stores versioned models trained in Snowflake or elsewhere as schema-level objects with metadata, metrics and aliases, and runs their methods from SQL or Python for batch inference.

nodes.title: Snowflake Model Serving in Snowpark Container Services
nodes.description: Deploys registry models as autoscaling CPU or GPU inference services with HTTP endpoints, with gateway-based traffic splitting for shadow and canary releases.

nodes.title: Snowflake multi-cluster warehouses
nodes.description: Adds and removes clusters of the same size automatically, according to a scaling policy, to absorb bursts of concurrent queries without queuing.

nodes.title: Snowflake Native App Framework
nodes.description: Packages data, code, Streamlit UIs, containers, agents and MCP servers as applications that consumers install and run in their own accounts through listings.

nodes.title: Snowflake native connectors (Snowflake Connectors for ServiceNow, Google Analytics, SharePoint, PostgreSQL and MySQL)
nodes.description: Connectors packaged as Snowflake Native Apps that ingest and refresh data from SaaS applications and databases incrementally, some using a customer-run agent for change data capture.

nodes.title: Snowflake network policies and network rules
nodes.description: Restrict which IP ranges, VPC endpoints or private endpoints can reach an account or user, and which external destinations workloads can reach.

nodes.title: Snowflake Notebooks in Workspaces
nodes.description: Jupyter-compatible notebooks in Snowsight Workspaces that run on Container Runtime CPU or GPU compute, with Git integration, a terminal and scheduling.

nodes.title: Snowflake object tagging
nodes.description: Schema-level tags with allowed values that are attached to objects and columns, inherited down the hierarchy, and used for classification, cost attribution and tag-based policies.

nodes.title: Observe by Snowflake
nodes.description: An observability platform for logs, metrics and traces, built on a Snowflake lakehouse and available standalone or paid for with Snowflake credits.

nodes.title: Snowflake Online Feature Store
nodes.description: Syncs feature views to a low-latency online store and serves them by key through a REST API, with stream and real-time feature views for sub-minute freshness.

nodes.title: Snowflake Open Catalog
nodes.description: A separate managed Apache Polaris service that acts as an Iceberg REST catalogue with central access control for Iceberg tables shared across engines.

nodes.title: Snowflake Open Data Sharing
nodes.description: Shares Iceberg tables as live, read-only data with external consumers outside Snowflake, who read them through standard Iceberg REST Catalog APIs using a programmatic access token.

nodes.title: Snowflake Openflow
nodes.description: A managed integration service, built on Apache NiFi, that runs prebuilt and custom connectors for databases, SaaS, streams and unstructured content in batch or streaming mode.

nodes.title: Snowflake organisations
nodes.description: Group multiple Snowflake accounts across regions and clouds under one organisation for account creation, organisation-wide usage views, organisation users and organisational listings.

nodes.title: pandas on Snowflake
nodes.description: A Modin-based pandas API that turns pandas operations on Snowflake data into SQL, and chooses per operation whether to run them locally or in Snowflake (hybrid execution).

nodes.title: pg_lake
nodes.description: An open-source Postgres extension from Snowflake that reads and writes Iceberg tables and Parquet files in object storage from Postgres.

nodes.title: Snowflake Postgres
nodes.description: Fully managed PostgreSQL instances, on versions 16 to 18, created and governed from Snowflake, running on dedicated Snowflake-managed machines with PgBouncer pooling and private networking.

nodes.title: Data mirroring for Snowflake Postgres
nodes.description: Continuously replicates Postgres tables or whole schemas into Snowflake tables from the write-ahead log, with sub-minute lag and source transaction boundaries kept.

nodes.title: Snowflake private connectivity (AWS PrivateLink, Azure Private Link, Google Cloud Private Service Connect)
nodes.description: Connects clients, internal stages and Snowflake-hosted endpoints to Snowflake over the cloud provider's private network rather than the public internet.

nodes.title: Snowflake projection policies
nodes.description: Stop a column from being returned in query output while still allowing it in joins, filters and aggregations.

nodes.title: Snowflake Query Acceleration Service
nodes.description: Offloads parts of large scans and filters in eligible queries to shared serverless compute, so outlier queries finish faster without enlarging the warehouse.

nodes.title: Snowflake Query History, Query Profile and query insights
nodes.description: Snowsight views of query history, operator-level execution plans and automatic insights, used to diagnose slow or expensive queries.

nodes.title: Snowflake replication and failover groups
nodes.description: Replicate databases, users, roles, warehouses, policies and integrations to accounts in other regions or clouds, with promotion on failover and client redirect through connection objects.

nodes.title: Snowflake resource monitors
nodes.description: Credit quotas on warehouses or the whole account that notify or suspend warehouses when thresholds are reached.

nodes.title: Snowflake persisted query results (result cache)
nodes.description: Returns the stored result of an identical earlier query, for 24 hours and up to 31 days with reuse, when the underlying data has not changed, without using warehouse compute.

nodes.title: Snowflake row access policies
nodes.description: Schema-level policies that decide, using the querying role and mapping tables, which rows of a table or view a query returns.

nodes.title: Snowflake Search Optimization Service
nodes.description: Builds and maintains a persistent search access path on chosen tables and columns, so point lookups, substring, semi-structured, geospatial and full-text SEARCH queries skip most micro-partitions.

nodes.title: Snowflake secrets
nodes.description: Schema-level secret objects that hold credentials, OAuth tokens and keys for integrations, UDFs, Openflow and container services, so code does not contain them.

nodes.title: Snowflake Secure Data Sharing
nodes.description: Shares live, read-only database objects with other Snowflake accounts through shares, without copying data, with consumers paying for their own compute.

nodes.title: Snowflake semantic views
nodes.description: Schema-level objects that define logical tables, relationships, facts, dimensions and metrics, queried with SQL and used by Cortex Analyst, agents and BI tools.

nodes.title: Snowflake semi-structured data types (VARIANT, OBJECT, ARRAY)
nodes.description: Stores JSON, Avro, ORC, Parquet and XML in VARIANT, OBJECT and ARRAY columns, extracting columns for pruning, and queries them with path notation and FLATTEN.

nodes.title: Snowflake sensitive data classification
nodes.description: Scans tables in databases with a classification profile, assigns semantic and privacy categories to sensitive columns, and can map them to your own tags automatically.

nodes.title: SnowConvert AI
nodes.description: A migration tool that assesses and converts SQL code and objects from Teradata, Oracle, SQL Server, Redshift, Synapse, BigQuery, Databricks SQL and other platforms to Snowflake.

nodes.title: Snowpark
nodes.description: DataFrame and function APIs for Python, Java and Scala that push processing down into Snowflake warehouses as SQL, plus runtimes for running that code in the engine.

nodes.title: Snowpark Connect for Apache Spark
nodes.description: Runs existing Spark DataFrame and Spark SQL code on Snowflake compute through the Spark Connect protocol, so there is no Spark cluster to manage.

nodes.title: Snowpark Container Services
nodes.description: Runs OCI container images as long-running services or finite jobs on Snowflake-managed compute pools, including GPU nodes, inside the account's security boundary.

nodes.title: Snowpark-optimized warehouses
nodes.description: Warehouses with much more memory per node, and configurable CPU architecture, for memory-intensive Snowpark, UDF and single-node ML training work.

nodes.title: Snowpipe
nodes.description: A serverless pipe that loads files continuously from stages as they arrive, triggered by cloud storage event notifications or REST calls.

nodes.title: Snowpipe Streaming
nodes.description: Ingests rows directly into tables through SDKs (Java, Python, Node.js) or a REST API, with no files, making data queryable within seconds.

nodes.title: Snowsight dashboards
nodes.description: Simple dashboards built from charts and tables of query results in Snowsight, shared with other Snowflake users.

nodes.title: Snowflake stages and directory tables
nodes.description: Internal and external stages hold files in object storage, and directory tables catalogue the staged files with metadata so unstructured content can be listed, governed and processed with SQL.

nodes.title: Snowflake storage lifecycle policies
nodes.description: Schema-level policies that archive table rows to cheaper COOL or COLD tiers, or delete them permanently, according to conditions such as age.

nodes.title: Streamlit in Snowflake
nodes.description: Hosts Streamlit Python apps as Snowflake objects, on warehouse or container runtimes, with access governed by Snowflake roles.

nodes.title: Snowflake streams
nodes.description: Track inserts, updates and deletes on tables, views and other objects since an offset, so downstream jobs process only the changes.

nodes.title: Snowflake synthetic data generation
nodes.description: The GENERATE_SYNTHETIC_DATA procedure creates statistically similar tables, with the same column names and types, from up to five source tables without linking output rows to real records.

nodes.title: Snowflake tasks and task graphs
nodes.description: Run SQL, procedures or code on a schedule, in dependency graphs, or when a stream has new data, on serverless or user-managed compute.

nodes.title: Snowflake Terraform provider
nodes.description: A Terraform provider for managing Snowflake accounts, warehouses, databases, roles, grants and policies as code.

nodes.title: Snowflake time-series functions (ASOF JOIN, TIME_SLICE, RESAMPLE)
nodes.description: SQL constructs for aligning, bucketing and joining time-stamped data, including ASOF JOIN and gap filling.

nodes.title: Snowflake Time Travel
nodes.description: Queries, clones or undrops tables, schemas and databases as they were at an earlier point within a retention period of up to 90 days.

nodes.title: Snowflake Trail (event tables, logging, tracing and metrics)
nodes.description: Collects logs, OpenTelemetry-style traces and metrics from UDFs, procedures, Snowpark, Native Apps, container services and pipelines into event tables, with Snowsight dashboards.

nodes.title: Snowflake Tri-Secret Secure
nodes.description: Combines a Snowflake-maintained key with a customer-managed key in the cloud provider's KMS to create the composite master key for account data, so revoking the customer key makes data unreadable.

nodes.title: Snowflake Trust Center
nodes.description: Runs scanner packages (Security Essentials, CIS Benchmarks, Threat Intelligence, AI Security) against accounts and reports violations, detections and at-risk entities.

nodes.title: Snowflake user-defined functions and stored procedures
nodes.description: Custom scalar, table and aggregate functions and stored procedures written in SQL, Snowflake Scripting, JavaScript, Python, Java or Scala that run inside Snowflake.

nodes.title: Snowflake Universal Search
nodes.description: Searches object metadata across the account, the Snowflake Marketplace and the Internal Marketplace in Snowsight, in natural language, filtered by the user's privileges.

nodes.title: Snowflake data unloading (COPY INTO <location>)
nodes.description: Writes query results or tables to files in internal or external stages as CSV, JSON or Parquet, optionally partitioned.

nodes.title: Virtual Private Snowflake (VPS)
nodes.description: The highest Snowflake edition, which runs a dedicated, isolated Snowflake deployment for a single customer, with its own metadata store and compute.

nodes.title: Snowflake virtual warehouses
nodes.description: Named clusters of compute, sized from X-Small to 6X-Large, that run SQL and Snowpark workloads against shared storage and suspend and resume automatically.

nodes.title: Snowflake Extension for Visual Studio Code
nodes.description: An IDE extension for connecting to Snowflake, running SQL and Snowpark code, and using CoCo from a local editor.

nodes.title: Snowsight Workspaces
nodes.description: A file-based editor in Snowsight for SQL, Python, notebooks, dbt projects, Streamlit apps and semantic views, with Git integration, sharing and AI code suggestions.

nodes.title: Snowflake zero-copy cloning
nodes.description: Creates instant writable copies of tables, schemas or databases that share micro-partitions with the source until either side changes.

nodes.title: Soda Cloud
nodes.description: Collaborative workspace for defining data contracts, running checks in pipelines and on schedules, monitoring metrics for anomalies and triaging data incidents.

nodes.title: Soda Core
nodes.description: Data quality and data contract verification engine that checks schema and data against YAML contracts from a CLI, Python or a pipeline.

nodes.title: Solidatus
nodes.description: Lineage modelling tool that combines automatically harvested technical lineage with business process lineage in versioned, bi-temporal models.

nodes.title: SQLFluff
nodes.description: Linter and auto-formatter for SQL that supports many dialects and dbt or Jinja templating.

nodes.title: SQLMesh
nodes.description: Transformation framework that understands SQL semantically, plans changes before applying them and uses virtual data environments to test and promote models without rebuilding tables.

nodes.title: Starburst Enterprise
nodes.description: Self-managed, supported Trino distribution for running federated and lakehouse SQL on Kubernetes in the customer's own environment.

nodes.title: Starburst Galaxy
nodes.description: Managed Trino-based query service that queries lake tables and federated sources in place, with Iceberg lake management, streaming ingest into live tables and built-in governance.

nodes.title: StarRocks
nodes.description: MPP analytical database with a vectorised engine, used for real-time analytics and as a fast query layer over Iceberg, Hudi, Delta and Paimon tables.

nodes.title: StarTree Cloud
nodes.description: Managed Apache Pinot service for low-latency, high-concurrency analytics on fresh event data, including user-facing and agent-facing applications.

nodes.title: Stibo Systems STEP
nodes.description: Multidomain MDM and product information management for product, customer, supplier and location data, with validation, enrichment and configurable hierarchies.

nodes.title: Streamlit
nodes.description: Python framework for building interactive data and AI web applications from scripts without front-end code.

nodes.title: Striim Cloud
nodes.description: Managed streaming integration service that loads an initial snapshot, then captures changes and processes them with continuous SQL queries before delivery to cloud targets.

nodes.title: Syndigo MDM
nodes.description: Master data management for product, customer, supplier and location records, alongside Syndigo's product information management and retailer content syndication.

nodes.title: Tableau Cloud
nodes.description: Hosted Tableau analytics service for building, sharing and embedding interactive dashboards, with Tableau Agent for natural-language questions, data preparation and authoring help.

nodes.title: Tableau Next
nodes.description: API-first agentic analytics product on Salesforce's Hyperforce that uses Data 360 as its data layer and Tableau Semantics as its semantic model.

nodes.title: Tableau Pulse
nodes.description: Metric-following experience in Tableau Cloud that defines metrics once and then sends followers automated summaries of trends, drivers and outliers in Slack, Teams, email and mobile.

nodes.title: Tamr
nodes.description: Machine-learning-led MDM that matches and enriches records with built-in external reference data to produce golden records, made available in real time.

nodes.title: Teradata Enterprise AgentStack
nodes.description: Suite for building, running and governing AI agents on Teradata, made up of AgentBuilder, Enterprise MCP, AgentEngine and AgentOps.

nodes.title: Teradata AI Studio
nodes.description: Umbrella environment for in-database analytics, open Python compute, ModelOps, vector storage and agent tooling on the Teradata platform.

nodes.title: Teradata Autonomous Knowledge Platform
nodes.description: Umbrella name for Teradata's platform of database, open-format storage access, analytics, vector and agent services, run either as Teradata Cloud or Teradata Factory.

nodes.title: Teradata Backup, Archive and Restore and Data Mover
nodes.description: Tools for backing up Teradata systems, restoring them, and copying tables and databases between systems for disaster recovery or environment refresh.

nodes.title: Teradata Bring Your Own Model (BYOM)
nodes.description: Database functions that score externally trained models, such as ONNX and PMML, in parallel inside Teradata without exporting data.

nodes.title: Teradata Cloud
nodes.description: Teradata-managed deployment of the platform on AWS, Azure and Google Cloud, combining always-on active compute with elastic compute that scales on demand over database and object-storage data.

nodes.title: Teradata Database
nodes.description: Shared-nothing MPP SQL database engine that underlies all Teradata deployments, with mixed-workload management, temporal tables and support for semi-structured data.

nodes.title: Teradata Elastic Python Compute
nodes.description: Managed, distributed Python environment based on Ray that runs ML, AI and data engineering code on CPUs or GPUs next to Teradata Database and open-format tables.

nodes.title: Teradata Enterprise MCP
nodes.description: Governed MCP server that exposes Teradata data, metadata, analytics, vector store and administration functions to AI agents as tools, bound to each user's identity and database roles.

nodes.title: Teradata Enterprise Vector Store
nodes.description: Vector storage and retrieval inside the Teradata platform, with hybrid keyword and semantic search across structured data and embeddings of text, images and audio.

nodes.title: Teradata Fabric
nodes.description: Query federation layer that joins data across Teradata systems and other engines such as Hive, Spark SQL, Oracle and BigQuery, pushing processing to where the data sits.

nodes.title: Teradata Factory
nodes.description: On-premises Teradata system on Dell compute and storage with NVIDIA GPUs, running warehouse, lakehouse and AI workloads together inside the customer's data centre.

nodes.title: Teradata in-database analytics functions
nodes.description: Large library of SQL functions for data preparation, statistics, machine learning, time-series and path analysis that run in parallel inside the database, also callable from Python and R.

nodes.title: Teradata ModelOps
nodes.description: Model lifecycle service that validates, deploys and monitors in-database and imported models, with drift alerts, a feature catalogue and audit trails of the data used.

nodes.title: Teradata Open Table Format support (Apache Iceberg and Delta Lake)
nodes.description: Ability for the Teradata engine to read and write Apache Iceberg and Delta Lake tables in object storage through external catalogues, alongside Native Object Store access to Parquet, CSV and JSON files.

nodes.title: Teradata Database security (roles, row-level security, encryption)
nodes.description: Built-in database controls for role-based privileges, row-level security constraints, column masking through views and functions, access logging and encryption.

nodes.title: Teradata Tera
nodes.description: Agentic workspace in which Teradata agents analyse data, write code, tune queries and run multi-step data tasks, grounded in governed metadata, lineage and policies.

nodes.title: Teradata Viewpoint
nodes.description: Web console for monitoring Teradata systems, queries, sessions and workloads and for managing workload rules.

nodes.title: HashiCorp Terraform
nodes.description: Infrastructure-as-code tool that declares infrastructure in HCL and creates, changes and destroys it through providers.

nodes.title: ThoughtSpot Analyst Studio
nodes.description: Data preparation and modelling environment with a SQL IDE, Python and R notebooks, data mash-ups and cached snapshots for repeated querying.

nodes.title: ThoughtSpot Analytics
nodes.description: Search- and AI-driven analytics service for business users, with governed models, Liveboards (interactive dashboards) and an embedding SDK.

nodes.title: ThoughtSpot Spotter
nodes.description: ThoughtSpot's AI analyst agent, which answers natural-language questions over governed models and investigates follow-ups, including over unstructured data.

nodes.title: Tinybird
nodes.description: Managed ClickHouse platform that ingests events and files, transforms them with SQL pipes and incremental materialised views, and publishes the results as authenticated HTTP API endpoints.

nodes.title: Tonic Structural
nodes.description: De-identifies and subsets structured production databases into realistic, referentially intact copies for development and testing.

nodes.title: Tonic Textual
nodes.description: Detects named entities in free text, documents and audio and redacts them or replaces them with consistent synthetic values.

nodes.title: Trino
nodes.description: Distributed SQL query engine that queries data in place across object storage, lakehouse tables and many databases through connectors.

nodes.title: Twilio Segment
nodes.description: Customer data platform that collects behavioural events through SDKs, validates them against tracking plans, unifies profiles and sends data to destinations, including from the warehouse.

nodes.title: Unity Catalog (open source)
nodes.description: Open-source catalogue for tables, volumes of files, functions and AI models, with an Iceberg REST and Hive Metastore compatible API.

nodes.title: Unstructured.io
nodes.description: Managed service that partitions documents into structured elements, then chunks and embeds them and loads them into vector stores and data platforms, from 20+ source connectors.

nodes.title: Varonis Data Security Platform
nodes.description: Classifies sensitive data, maps permissions and monitors activity across file shares, SaaS, cloud and databases to remove excess access and detect threats to data.

nodes.title: vLLM
nodes.description: High-throughput inference and serving engine for large language models, with an OpenAI-compatible API.

nodes.title: Vortex
nodes.description: Extensible columnar file format and toolkit with pluggable encodings and compression, designed for fast random access and scans on object storage.

nodes.title: WarpStream
nodes.description: Kafka-compatible streaming service that runs as stateless agents in the customer's cloud account and writes data directly to object storage, managed by Confluent.

nodes.title: Weaviate Cloud
nodes.description: Managed deployment of the Weaviate vector database with hybrid keyword and vector search, hosted embeddings and an agentic Query Agent.

nodes.title: Weights & Biases
nodes.description: Experiment tracking, hyperparameter sweeps, artefact versioning and a model registry (W&B Models), plus tracing and evaluation of LLM and agent applications (W&B Weave).

nodes.title: Workiva
nodes.description: Cloud platform for financial, regulatory and sustainability reporting that links reported figures to their source data and produces filings in formats such as XBRL and ESEF.

nodes.title: Separate read models
nodes.description: Separate the models used to write data from models shaped for reading, and keep the read models in sync.

nodes.title: Data fabric
nodes.description: Integrate distributed data through a metadata-driven layer that automates discovery, integration and governance across sources.

nodes.title: Data lake
nodes.description: A store of raw data in open files of any structure, with schema applied when the data is read.

nodes.title: Data marts
nodes.description: Subject- or department-specific sets of data shaped for one group of users.

nodes.title: Data mesh
nodes.description: Decentralise data ownership to business domains that publish data products on a shared self-service platform under federated governance.

nodes.title: Data Vault
nodes.description: Model integrated history with hubs, links and satellites so new sources can be added without rework.

nodes.title: Data warehouse
nodes.description: A central store of integrated, historical data, modelled for analysis and reporting.

nodes.title: Dimensional modelling
nodes.description: Model data as fact tables of measurements surrounded by dimension tables of context.

nodes.title: ELT
nodes.description: Extract and load raw data into the platform first, then transform it there.

nodes.title: ETL
nodes.description: Extract data, transform it in a separate engine, then load the result into the target.

nodes.title: Feature, training and inference pipelines
nodes.description: Split an ML system into independent feature, training and inference pipelines that share a feature store and model registry.

nodes.title: Kappa architecture
nodes.description: Treat all data as streams and rebuild state by replaying the log, using a single processing path.

nodes.title: Lakehouse
nodes.description: Warehouse-style tables, transactions and governance on open formats in object storage, shared by many engines.

nodes.title: Lambda architecture
nodes.description: Run a batch layer and a speed layer in parallel and merge their results for serving.

nodes.title: Medallion architecture
nodes.description: Organise data in layers of increasing refinement, typically bronze (raw), silver (cleaned) and gold (business-ready).

nodes.title: Metadata-driven pipelines
nodes.description: Run one generic ingestion or transformation pipeline driven by control tables that list hundreds of sources and how to load each.

nodes.title: One big table
nodes.description: Denormalise data into wide tables to simplify and speed up analytical queries.

nodes.title: Shift-left data quality and governance
nodes.description: Move quality checks, contracts and governance controls upstream to where data is produced.

nodes.title: Slowly changing dimensions
nodes.description: Track changes to descriptive attributes over time, for example by overwriting values or versioning rows.

nodes.title: Transactional outbox
nodes.description: Write events to an outbox table in the same transaction as the business change, then publish them reliably.

nodes.title: Write-audit-publish
nodes.description: Write new data to an isolated location, check it, and only then publish it to consumers.

nodes.title: AI engineer
nodes.description: Builds applications and agents on foundation models and enterprise data.

nodes.title: Analytics engineer
nodes.description: Turns raw data into tested, documented, analysis-ready models.

nodes.title: Business user
nodes.description: Uses data, reports and AI assistants to make decisions, without deep technical skills.

nodes.title: Chief data officer
nodes.description: Accountable for the organisation's data strategy, value, risk and governance.

nodes.title: Data analyst
nodes.description: Answers business questions through analysis, dashboards and reports.

nodes.title: Data architect
nodes.description: Designs the data platform and how data flows, is modelled and is governed across the organisation.

nodes.title: Data engineer
nodes.description: Builds and operates the pipelines that ingest, transform and deliver data.

nodes.title: Data product owner
nodes.description: Owns the value, roadmap and consumers of one or more data products.

nodes.title: Data scientist
nodes.description: Explores data and builds statistical and machine learning models.

nodes.title: Data steward
nodes.description: Looks after the definition, quality and proper use of data in a business domain.

nodes.title: FinOps practitioner
nodes.description: Tracks, allocates and optimises what the data platform costs.

nodes.title: ML engineer
nodes.description: Takes models to production and keeps them running reliably.

nodes.title: Data platform engineer
nodes.description: Builds and runs the shared data platform and its self-service tooling.

nodes.title: Risk and compliance officer
nodes.description: Needs assurance, with evidence, that data controls meet regulatory and internal requirements.

nodes.title: Security and privacy officer
nodes.description: Protects data and makes sure it is used lawfully.

nodes.title: Software engineer
nodes.description: Builds applications that produce data for the platform or consume data from it.

nodes.title: Agentic process automation
nodes.description: AI agents complete multi-step business tasks using enterprise data and tools under controls.

nodes.title: Application data publishing
nodes.description: Application teams publish their data to the platform through versioned events and change capture under agreed contracts, so downstream consumers do not break when applications change.

nodes.title: Churn prediction
nodes.description: Score customers regularly by likelihood to leave so teams can act before they do.

nodes.title: Conversational analytics for business users
nodes.description: Business users ask questions of governed data in plain language and get trustworthy answers.

nodes.title: Credit decisioning
nodes.description: Score credit applications and decide to approve, decline or refer them, with reasons, fairness checks and model risk controls.

nodes.title: Customer 360
nodes.description: Give every channel a single, trusted view of each customer.

nodes.title: Customer-facing analytics
nodes.description: Give external customers fast, secure analytics inside a product.

nodes.title: Data sharing and monetisation
nodes.description: Share or sell data products to partners and customers under agreed terms.
aliases: data as a product for partners

nodes.title: Demand forecasting
nodes.description: Forecast demand by product, location and time to plan stock, staff and supply.

nodes.title: Document data extraction
nodes.description: Extract fields and tables from invoices, claims, contracts and forms into business systems, with people reviewing uncertain results.

nodes.title: Self-service domain onboarding
nodes.description: Give a new domain or product team a governed workspace, path to live and budget on the shared platform within a day.

nodes.title: Enterprise management reporting
nodes.description: Produce trusted, consistent KPIs and management reports across the organisation.

nodes.title: Real-time fraud detection
nodes.description: Score transactions in milliseconds and block or flag suspicious ones.

nodes.title: IoT predictive maintenance
nodes.description: Analyse sensor telemetry to predict equipment failures before they happen.

nodes.title: Marketing audience activation
nodes.description: Build audiences from platform data and sync them to marketing and advertising tools.

nodes.title: Operational reporting
nodes.description: Report on current operations within minutes of events happening.

nodes.title: Platform cost management and chargeback
nodes.description: Attribute, forecast and control what the data platform costs, and recover it from the teams and products that use it.

nodes.title: Legacy warehouse migration
nodes.description: Move from an on-premises warehouse or Hadoop estate to a cloud data platform.

nodes.title: Privacy rights handling
nodes.description: Find, report and erase an individual's data across the estate within legal deadlines.

nodes.title: Knowledge assistant
nodes.description: A generative AI assistant that answers questions from internal documents, with citations.

nodes.title: Personalised recommendations
nodes.description: Recommend products or content to each user in real time.

nodes.title: Regulatory reporting
nodes.description: Produce accurate, auditable and reproducible submissions to regulators.

nodes.title: Security and log analytics
nodes.description: Collect and analyse large volumes of logs to detect threats and investigate incidents.

nodes.title: Self-service BI
nodes.description: Analysts and business users explore governed data and build their own reports with trusted metrics.

nodes.title: Sensitive data protection
nodes.description: Know where sensitive and personal data is across the platform, control who can reach it through one set of policies, and prove it to auditors.

nodes.title: AI and model governance
nodes.description: How well the organisation knows its AI systems, assesses their risks and impacts, controls their behaviour and evidences this to regulators and customers.

nodes.title: Analytics and BI
nodes.description: How consistently people across the organisation explore, report on and act on data using shared definitions and governed tools.

nodes.title: Compute and workload management
nodes.description: How well compute is provisioned, isolated, scaled and tuned so that workloads meet performance targets at a known cost.

nodes.title: Data products
nodes.description: How far data is managed as products with accountable owners, known consumers, explicit contracts and service levels.

nodes.title: Data quality and observability
nodes.description: How systematically the organisation defines, measures, monitors and fixes the fitness of data for its intended uses.

nodes.title: Data sharing
nodes.description: How safely and efficiently data is shared between teams and with external parties without unnecessary copies.

nodes.title: FinOps
nodes.description: How well the organisation understands, allocates and controls what the data platform costs, relative to the value it delivers.

nodes.title: Generative AI
nodes.description: How safely and reliably the organisation builds, evaluates and runs applications that use language models and agents with its own data.

nodes.title: Governance operating model
nodes.description: How clearly the rules, roles and controls for managing data are defined, implemented on the platform and evidenced.

nodes.title: Ingestion and integration
nodes.description: How reliably, quickly and safely the organisation brings data from source systems into the platform and keeps it in step with them.

nodes.title: Lineage
nodes.description: How completely and automatically the organisation can show where data came from, how it was changed and what depends on it.

nodes.title: Master and reference data
nodes.description: How consistently core business entities and shared code lists are identified, matched and maintained across systems.

nodes.title: Metadata and catalogue
nodes.description: How completely and accurately data assets are described, findable and connected through metadata, for people and for machines.

nodes.title: ML development
nodes.description: How repeatably the organisation turns data into trained, evaluated and documented models.

nodes.title: MLOps
nodes.description: How automatically and safely models are released, run, monitored and improved in production.

nodes.title: Orchestration
nodes.description: How dependably the organisation schedules, sequences and recovers the jobs that move and transform data.

nodes.title: Path to live
nodes.description: How safely, quickly and repeatably changes to data and AI workloads move from a developer's first commit to production.

nodes.title: Platform migration and portability
nodes.description: How safely and predictably the organisation moves workloads, code and data to new platforms, and how freely it can choose where the platform runs.

nodes.title: Platform self-service
nodes.description: How far teams can obtain, run and observe what they need on the shared platform without waiting for a central team.

nodes.title: Privacy
nodes.description: How reliably the organisation meets its obligations to the people its data describes, from purpose and consent to rights requests and de-identification.

nodes.title: Real-time and streaming
nodes.description: How well the organisation moves, processes and queries data continuously, with predictable latency and correct results, instead of in scheduled batches.

nodes.title: Resilience and recovery
nodes.description: How well the platform withstands and recovers from data loss, corruption, ransomware and outages within agreed targets.

nodes.title: Security and access control
nodes.description: How well data is protected from unauthorised access, loss and misuse, from identity through fine-grained access to threat detection.

nodes.title: Data serving
nodes.description: How well curated data reaches applications, people and operational tools at the latency, volume and reliability they need.

nodes.title: Specialised data
nodes.description: How well the organisation stores, governs and analyses data that needs specialised types, indexes or engines, such as time series, location, graphs, searchable text, media, logs and bitemporal history.

nodes.title: Storage and table management
nodes.description: How well data is kept in durable, open, maintained tables that many engines can read, update and trust.

nodes.title: Transformation engineering
nodes.description: How consistently transformation logic is written, tested, reused and run efficiently, from raw data to tables ready for use.

nodes.description: Amazon's cloud, with separate managed services for each part of the data and AI stack.

nodes.title: ClickHouse
nodes.description: An open-source columnar database for real-time analytics, also sold as a managed cloud service.

nodes.description: A hybrid data platform for on-premises and cloud deployments that grew out of the Hadoop ecosystem.

nodes.title: Databricks
